messages.text: single mom here with a 2 year old. I make about $450 a week at a warehouse. what can we get?

Thanks for sharing that. I can check food assistance (SNAP), WIC, and TennCare/CoverKids for you and your 2-year-old. I need two more things first:

1. How much is your rent or mortgage each month? Do you pay separately for heating or cooling, for other utilities like electric or water, or for only a phone?
2. Do you pay for child care so you can work? If so, about how much each month?
rent is $750 a month. we pay electric and gas separately, gas is for heat. no child care costs, my mom watches her for free

You'll probably qualify for help from all three programs. These are estimates, and only the agencies decide.

**Food assistance (SNAP): likely, about $327 a month (estimate)**
- The screening counted your pay as about $1,935 a month before taxes. It is under the limit for a household of 2 (about $2,345 a month).
- Your rent and gas and electric bills lower the income SNAP counts. That's why the estimate is fairly high.
- The utility figure used was the latest published one, from before 9/30/2026. Newer figures weren't available, so your amount could change a little.
- Savings: the federal limit is $3,000 in cash and bank accounts. I didn't ask about yours.
- Apply at [OneDHS](https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp?id=start_snap_application) or call 866-311-4287.
- Sources: [USDA's FY 2027 SNAP limits](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/allotment/cola), [SNAP eligibility rules](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/recipient/eligibility), and [7 CFR 273.10](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-273.10).

**WIC: likely, for your daughter**
- She is under 5, and your income is under WIC's limit of $3,337 a month for 2 people.
- The clinic will do a short health and nutrition check.
- Apply at a local health department clinic or call 1-800-342-5942. More info is on the [Tennessee WIC site](https://www.tn.gov/health/wic.html).
- Sources: [WIC income limits for July 2026 to June 2027](https://www.fns.usda.gov/wic/fr-042926) and [7 CFR 246.2](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-246.2).

**TennCare/CoverKids**
- **Your daughter: likely.** The limit for a child her age is $2,561 a month for 2 people.
- **You: unlikely.** The limit for parents is $1,804 a month, and you're a bit over it. You can still apply.
- Apply at [TennCare Connect](https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/) or call 855-259-0701.
- Source: [TennCare Eligibility Reference Guide](https://www.tn.gov/coverkids/coverkids/redirect-income-guidelines.html).

One thing to check: I didn't ask your age, so I entered you as an adult. If you're under 18 or over 60, tell me, because that could change the result.

You can also dial **211** for free help applying locally.

Thanks. Age 27 doesn't change anything, so the results stand.

- **Food assistance (SNAP):** likely, about $327 a month (estimate).
- **WIC:** likely, for your daughter.
- **TennCare/CoverKids:** likely for your daughter. Unlikely for you, but you can still apply.

I'd start with SNAP, since it has the biggest dollar amount. Apply at [OneDHS](https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp?id=start_snap_application) or call 866-311-4287. Then call 1-800-342-5942 for WIC and 855-259-0701 for TennCare. If you want help with any of it, dial 211.

Please report your pay and household details accurately on each application. Only the state agencies decide who gets help.
